title: Rate-limit + cache profile metadata fetches to protect model registry under high QPS
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Improves resiliency of Quantization Profile Library by caching and rate-limiting profile metadata reads from the model registry to prevent thundering herd under high QPS; adds visibility via new metrics and structured logs.
description:
Context: During beta traffic spikes we observed elevated 5xx on the control plane path that resolves route-level quantization settings. Root cause was a thundering herd of profile metadata reads to the model registry when many routes/tenants were simultaneously evaluating quantization_profile_ref (especially on cold cache / rollout events). This PR adds defensive caching and outbound rate limiting on the registry metadata fetch path so that a single hot tenant or a deployment restart cannot overload the registry. The goal is to keep default behavior unchanged and only reduce registry load + isolate failure modes.

What changed: (1) Added an L1 in-process cache for profile metadata (profile_id -> resolved metadata + validation summary) with TTL + negative caching for NotFound/Incompatible responses to avoid repeated retries. (2) Added a per-pod token-bucket rate limiter for outbound registry calls (separate buckets for metadata vs artifact HEAD) with a conservative default and configuration via env/flags. (3) Added singleflight-style request coalescing so concurrent requests for the same profile_id share one in-flight fetch rather than N identical calls. (4) Implemented jittered backoff + bounded retry for transient registry errors; on rate-limit exhaustion we fail open to safe fallback behavior (treat as unresolved and proceed with baseline precision), but we emit explicit resolution_outcome=rate_limited so it’s visible. (5) Added metrics + logs: registry_profile_metadata_fetch_total{status}, registry_profile_metadata_fetch_latency_ms, registry_profile_metadata_cache_hit_total, registry_profile_metadata_singleflight_shared_total, registry_profile_metadata_rate_limited_total, and control_plane_quant_profile_resolution_outcome{applied,fallback,disabled,rate_limited,error}. (6) Tests: unit coverage for cache TTL/negative cache, rate limiter enforcement, singleflight coalescing, and a concurrency test verifying that 500 parallel resolves generate <=1 registry fetch per profile per TTL window.

Notes/Behavior: - This is intentionally scoped to metadata fetches (profile JSON + compatibility summary), not the larger artifact download path used by runtime. - TTL default is 60s with a 10% jitter to reduce synchronized expirations. - Negative cache TTL is 15s to avoid masking newly published profiles for too long. - Fail-open semantics (fallback to baseline) align with serving standards: if we cannot deterministically confirm applicability we do not apply the profile.

Operational impact: This should significantly reduce registry QPS during rollouts and after pod restarts. Dashboards/alerts can now key off registry_profile_metadata_rate_limited_total and resolution_outcome=rate_limited to catch misconfiguration. See SUP-27488 for customer-visible symptoms and the incident thread for timeline.

Checklist: Added unit + concurrency tests; updated internal runbook snippet for diagnosing registry pressure; verified no behavior change when quantization profiles are disabled; validated in staging with synthetic 2k RPS resolve load and confirmed registry QPS reduction >90% with stable p95 policy eval latency.

review_conversation: Quentin Harris: Can we ensure negative caching doesn’t hide newly published profiles too long? Suggest keeping it short and only for 404 / invalid schema cases.

Benji Okafor: Updated negative TTL to 15s (configurable) and limited it to NotFound + SchemaInvalid + Incompatible. Also added a metric for negative_cache_hit_total so we can observe if it’s masking anything.
Mina Haddad: Fail-open to baseline makes sense, but we need an explicit outcome so routing/debugging can distinguish ‘fallback due to incompatibility’ vs ‘fallback due to rate limiting/error’.
Benji Okafor: Added resolution_outcome=rate_limited and resolution_outcome=error and wired through to structured logs + metrics; updated README section on outcomes.
Connor O'Brien: Please add guardrails so the limiter can’t be configured to 0 and brick all profile resolution; also add a runbook note for registry pressure.
Benji Okafor: Added min=1 rps validation with startup warning + defaulting; added runbook doc and linked in README.
Ethan Park: Singleflight implementation looks good; can you add a concurrency test to ensure one fetch per profile per TTL window?
Benji Okafor: Added TestSingleflightCoalescesConcurrentFetches with 500 goroutines; asserts <=1 fetch for same profile_id and validates shared counter metric increments.
Quentin Harris: Approved after negative-cache tweaks and metrics.
Connor O'Brien: Approved; please follow up with alert thresholds once we have baseline data.
